rows.source: HSE Work at Height Regulations guidance
rows.verified: The Work at Height Regulations aim to prevent death and injury caused by falls from height.

rows.source: HSE Work at Height Regulations guidance
rows.verified: Employers and people controlling work at height must assess the risks.

rows.source: HSE Work at Height Regulations guidance
rows.verified: Work should be properly planned before it starts.

rows.source: HSE Work at Height Regulations guidance
rows.verified: Work at height should be appropriately supervised.

rows.source: HSE Work at Height Regulations guidance
rows.verified: People carrying out the work should be competent for the task.

rows.source: HSE Work at Height Regulations guidance
rows.verified: The correct type of access and protective equipment should be selected.

rows.source: HSE Work at Height Regulations guidance
rows.verified: Planning effort and controls should reflect the complexity and risk of the activity.

rows.source: HSE Work at Height Regulations guidance
rows.verified: Workers must take reasonable care and cooperate with the dutyholder's safety arrangements.

rows.source: HSE Work at Height Regulations guidance
rows.verified: Fall risk depends on task height, duration, surface, edges, openings, fragility, weather, access, equipment, rescue planning and worker competence.

rows.source: HSE Work at Height Regulations guidance
rows.verified: General work-at-height guidance does not prove controls at a specific location or quantify an exact parcel-level fall probability.

rows.source: HSE RIDDOR incident-reporting guidance
rows.verified: A RIDDOR report is required only where an accident is work-related and results in a reportable outcome.

rows.source: HSE RIDDOR incident-reporting guidance
rows.verified: Work-related deaths resulting from accidents are reportable, subject to the stated exceptions.

rows.source: HSE RIDDOR incident-reporting guidance
rows.verified: Specified injuries include most fractures other than those to fingers, thumbs and toes.

rows.source: HSE RIDDOR incident-reporting guidance
rows.verified: Specified injuries also include listed amputations, serious eye damage and certain crush injuries.

rows.source: HSE RIDDOR incident-reporting guidance
rows.verified: Serious burns meeting the regulatory criteria can be reportable.

rows.source: HSE RIDDOR incident-reporting guidance
rows.verified: Certain occupational diseases and gas incidents are within the reporting framework.

rows.source: HSE RIDDOR incident-reporting guidance
rows.verified: Dangerous occurrences are specified high-potential incidents listed in Schedule 2.

rows.source: HSE RIDDOR incident-reporting guidance
rows.verified: Reporting allows enforcing authorities and businesses to learn from incidents and support prevention.

rows.source: HSE RIDDOR incident-reporting guidance
rows.verified: RIDDOR applicability depends on the exact event, work relationship, injured person, diagnosis, outcome, timing and regulatory category.

rows.source: HSE RIDDOR incident-reporting guidance
rows.verified: A report, absence of a report or area-level incident statistic does not prove site safety or establish an exact parcel-level event probability.
